value.rationale: Critical-density Gabor systems lack uniform lower frame bounds; their spectral distribution quantifies the frequency of near-singular Zak fibers, beyond zero count or essential spectral extrema. For the canonical quadratic B-spline this theorem identifies the unique interior nondegenerate saddle, exact logarithmic blowup coefficient, contrasting endpoint laws, a fully calculable distribution, and regularized inverse conditioning. These are meaningful global spectral invariants and nonroutine qualitative structure rather than a restatement of the classical Zak-zero theorem.
